analysis.investment_thesis: Indobell fails the Magic Formula on both counts: ROE of 0.21% implies near-zero return on capital, while a P/E of 20 on such anemic profitability signals a poor earnings yield. Cheap-and-good is the mandate; this is expensive-and-bad.
key_strengths: High promoter holding at 65% signals skin in the game
50+ year operating history (since 1972) in insulation niche
Tiny INR 45 Cr cap offers re-rating optionality if ROIC ever inflects
key_risks: ROE of 0.21% indicates capital is essentially idle — fails ROIC test
P/E of 20 on negligible earnings = earnings yield ~5%, below 6% threshold
Microcap in commoditized industrial insulation — no pricing power
red_flags: ROE <1% is effectively no return on capital
Negligible DII participation (1.79%) — institutions avoid for a reason
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula requires ranking high on BOTH earnings yield (EBIT/EV) and return on capital (EBIT/invested capital). Indobell flunks both. A 0.21% ROE means essentially no earnings are generated on the equity base — a business earning nothing on capital cannot be a quality compounder regardless of price. Paying 20x earnings for such negligible profitability yields roughly 5%, well below my 12%+ attractive threshold.

Systematic investing means no exceptions. There is no scenario where Indobell ranks well on the two-factor screen: it sits in the bottom quartile on ROIC and the bottom half on earnings yield. The 65% promoter stake and long operating history don't overcome the arithmetic. Pass and redeploy capital to names that are both cheap AND good.
